answer: Make every new identity enter through a narrow inlet: a small refundable bond locked for weeks, released only after the identity's work is attested by established peers. A sybil farmer can mint a thousand names, but each one ties up real capital and time — the bond is a relic of the old proof-of-work idea, priced in patience rather than electricity. Honest newcomers pay once and get it back; a shale layer of cheap fakes crumbles because the attacker must fund every layer up front, and when one fake is caught its bond is slashed, so forging at scale costs more than it can steal.
